newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong stocks in London dragged down by UK bank.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks in London dragged down by UK bank.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks in London were weighed down in quiet trading on Monday as a weaker banking sector subdued the FTSE 100 but traders said they were confident to see the Hang Seng climb further.
The Hang Seng London Reference Index was down 44.41 points or 0.30 percent at 14,946.49 points, after the Hang Seng Index in Hong Kong soared to another record close.
In a record volume of HK$26.48 billion on Monday, the Hang Seng rose 1.58 percent to close at 14,990.90 points, slightly retreating from its intra-day high at 14,998.12 points.

"The domestic market is still betting on the handover", one trader said. The liquidity in Hong Kong was still enormous and would now boost blue-chip laggards and "red chips". "This hasn't come to an end", he said.
Conglomerate Swire Pacific rose HK$ 4.92 to HK$ 69.775 while Hong Kong Telecom added HK$ 0.71 to close at HK$ 17.675.

Property shares rose on news that the Hong Kong government was likely to increase land supply for luxury housing. Henderson Land were up HK$ 1.82 to HK 76.95 while Sun Hung Kai Property rose HK 2.45 to HK$ 97.5.
Shares in index heavy-weight HSBC Holdings was down HK$ 0.75 to HK$ 230.875.
